unit.why: A homiletic passage built around brief anecdotal exempla: the Besht nearly falling from his level through the 'erev rav', R. Levi Yitzhak of Berdichev falling from his level for half a year through persecution by opponents (with the Maggid of Kozienice's comment), and the author's own experience of renewal through tefillin and prayer.
unit.boundary_note: narrative is minimal and wrapped in an extended homiletic frame; borderline with saying_or_teaching

stories.start_quote: ובאמת יאמינו לי אחיי ורעיי ידידי עליון
stories.end_quote: נעשה ברי' חדשה בלא חטא ועון אכי״ר
stories.summary_en: The author teaches that tests and despondency come upon the righteous. His examples are the Besht, who nearly fell from his level through the 'erev rav' and was strengthened from Heaven, and R. Levi Yitzhak of Berdichev, who fell from his level for over half a year through persecution by opponents. The Maggid of Kozienice explains that Levi Yitzhak did this on purpose to bring down the heavenly princes. The author then tells how he himself was renewed through tefillin, prayer and study.

tags.why: The anecdotes serve a homily on tests and on a verse/midrash about R. Hanina bar Papa
